test_title: PYST 5: SSC CGL 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 13th_September_2025_Shift_2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following industry pairs is **correctly **grouped as heavy industries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shipbuilding and Automobile**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Heavy industries** are characterized by the production of large-scale goods or machinery requiring significant capital investment, energy, and raw materials.
 
• **Shipbuilding and Automobile** industries are correctly classified as heavy industries due to their large-scale operations, heavy machinery usage, and production of durable goods.
 
• Shipbuilding involves the construction of ships and other sea vessels, requiring extensive infrastructure, labor, and advanced engineering techniques.
 
• The automobile industry focuses on manufacturing vehicles, which involves complex processes such as designing, assembling, and testing heavy machinery and components.
 
• Both industries significantly contribute to the economic development and infrastructure of a nation, providing employment opportunities and driving technological advancements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Industry Sectors in India**

 
 
• Primary Sector (Extraction & Agriculture)
 
 
• Agriculture & Allied: Food processing, dairy, fishing, forestry, horticulture.
 
• Mining & Minerals: Coal, iron ore, steel, cement, oil & gas. 
 
 
 
• Secondary Sector (Manufacturing & Construction)
 
 
• Manufacturing: Automotive, textiles, electronics, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, engineering goods.
 
• Construction: Real estate, infrastructure (roads, ports). 
 
 
 
• Tertiary Sector (Services)
 
 
• IT & BPM: Software services, IT outsourcing, tech consulting.
 
• Financial Services: Banking, insurance, FinTech, NBFCs.
 
• Healthcare & Education: Hospitals, medical devices, training.
 
• FMCG: Fast-moving consumer goods (food, personal care).
 
• Telecom & Media: Mobile networks, digital content.
 
• Tourism & Hospitality: Hotels, travel, aviation.
